items.title: Make canonical propagation preserve and self-heal consumer-owned safety overlays
items.why: The mandatory start sync overwrote all five documented PromoGrind runtime overrides and made the exact contracts shipped in S123 fail before product work began. The existing checker detects some drift only after imports crash and its hard-coded surface omits newly propagated session-floor files.
evidence: npm test: 3 failed files, 6 failed assertions, 1 import-failed suite after start-canon-sync
npm run test:session-invariants: first public-revenue provenance assertion failed
git diff shows regressions in context-meter, context-verdicts, sil-forecaster, scheduled-write admission, and startup renderer
scripts/check-runtime-pack-compatibility.mjs hard-codes 35 paths but this sync also introduced session-floor-items.mjs and token-cost-tier.mjs and changed session-floor.mjs
items.recipe: Extract a project-owned runtime overlay contract with protected paths and semantic probes. Add a conservative reconciler that restores the committed local version only when the working copy is byte-identical to canonical upstream and the committed version differs, refusing to touch user edits. Discover newly propagated changed files from live Git/upstream intersection, make compatibility reporting survive broken imports, run reconcile immediately after Canon sync through the repo-local protocol, and emit signed Ark cargo requesting an upstream consumer-overlay contract.

L1.recipe: Restore the five known overrides and rerun focused tests.

L2.recipe: Add protected-path manifest, conservative reconcile planning, check/apply CLI, and focused fixtures.

L3.recipe: L2 plus source-derived changed-file inventory, crash-safe compatibility receipts, repo-local start integration, full behavioral verification, and signed upstream cargo.

items.title: Replace synthetic social proof with an inspectable, provenance-enforced public evidence plane
items.axis: trust / UX / security / feedback loop / public claims
items.why: PromoGrind promises a sober, evidence-led operator product, but its pricing and landing surfaces present invented live activity, named testimonials, outcome amounts, competitor prices, and categorical legal assertions as facts. The source-derived public-claims receipt says green because its rules do not model endorsement or comparison provenance.
evidence: PricingPage.jsx contains a rotating fake activity feed with states, books, outcomes, amounts, and minute timestamps
PricingPage.jsx and public/landing/index.html contain the same three named testimonials and $340 first-week / $1,200-per-month claims
PricingPage.jsx, public/compliance/index.html, and comparison pages contain categorical legal or unsourced competitor-price claims
node scripts/check-public-claims.mjs --json reports ok=true, findings=[], checkedFiles=319
items.recipe: Delete synthetic user/activity claims everywhere. Replace them with a source-derived Evidence You Can Inspect surface built only from first-party capability and validation facts. Extend the public-claims engine with endorsement-provenance, simulated-live-activity, absolute-legality, and external-price rules; require explicit evidence metadata for any future testimonial; cover React and static HTML fixtures; render and visually inspect desktop/mobile dark/light pricing states.

L1.recipe: Remove the known fake feed/testimonials and categorical legal answer.

L2.recipe: L1 plus evidence cards and scanner rules across React/static surfaces.

L3.recipe: L2 plus structured provenance contract, adversarial fixtures, complete public-surface cleanup, rendered-pixel QA, and a content-addressed receipt.

Render tier cards, trial language, comparison rows, and disabled/beta states from it; never promise a disabled capability. Add parity tests against featureFlags/launchState/auth mappings and make unproved checkout states offer a waitlist or free workspace path instead of a subscription promise.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a shared plan/entitlement catalog and component tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus launch-capability binding, fail-closed availability states, parity receipts, and accessible pricing interactions.

items.title: Declare and enforce a truthful Obelisk-hybrid identity boundary before launch
items.axis: identity / security / ecosystem integration / release architecture
items.why: The project has Obelisk callback and Passport scaffolding but declares no obeliskArchitecture, while normal signup/sign-in/recovery still route directly through project-local Supabase auth. A hidden hybrid is not a release architecture and cannot satisfy CANON-045.
evidence: context/PROJECT_STATUS.json has no obeliskArchitecture field
src/auth.js owns primary email/password auth and recovery
src/ObeliskLogin.jsx and src/obelisk-callback.js exist but are not the declared identity boundary
release gate classifies Obelisk architecture and founder launch approval red
items.recipe: Declare `obeliskArchitecture: hybrid` in canonical status and a machine-readable identity contract. Make public auth entry points present Obelisk as the studio identity path, label local Supabase auth as an explicit FORGE compatibility path, preserve callback receipt verification, and add a launch contract that fails if architecture is absent or public auth silently becomes local-only. Do not claim Obelisk production readiness without external verification.

L1.recipe: Declare hybrid architecture and surface Obelisk at auth entry points.

L2.recipe: L1 plus one identity contract, callback receipt semantics, and local-compatibility labeling.

L3.recipe: L2 plus fail-closed release checks, recovery/logout/session flow coverage, and public agent-readable identity metadata.

Reuse an existing footer when present, otherwise add one accessible footer before body close; inject one exact linked proprietary identity line without duplicating navigation. Cover every public HTML source, bind the checker into release verification, and visually inspect representative landing, calculator, article, and legal pages at desktop/mobile.
